session: v0.4.0 Linux BLE live backend, supervised read-path validation
mode: read-only: no D7, no 0E, no allow_mutating, no configuration change, no frame replay

host.bluetooth: active; two controllers present. BlueZ powered its default controller for the scan; the lab dongle was never used, and the default controller was returned to its original powered-off state at the end of the session

candidate.name_pattern: ARMOR-X Pro_11 (exact name redacted in public artefacts)

scan.note: addresses are kept only in local runtime artefacts and never in this document, the repository or the PR

identity.note: read today from the device; the historically recorded values are confirmed, not assumed

gatt.independent_enumerator: read-only bleak enumeration, no writes and no subscriptions

service_under_test.remark: an unusual but genuinely advertised service; it is not a decode artefact of the toolkit

gatt.handle_drift: the ATT handles read one lower than the values recorded in the 2026-09-26 session (116/118 versus 117/119); the descriptors and properties are the same, so this is recorded as an observation, not an error

privacy.checked_by: direct inspection of the written baseline plus the same scan applied to the read artefacts

image_comparison.against: the research client's saved output from the 2026-09-27 physical sessions

live_rerun.detail: three LE create-connection attempts on the lab dongle failed with COMMAND_DISALLOWED_ERROR after the advertisement was seen; adapter ownership was restored automatically. Not retried further, because the byte-level comparison against the client's stored output already covers the comparison this phase asks for
live_rerun.independence_note: the reassembly implementations differ: the research client concatenates fragments in arrival order, the toolkit reassembles by fragment index and refuses conflicting duplicates

research_cross_check.preamble_note: the research client sends 0B, EF, D4 and E2 before D6; the toolkit sends D6 alone and still received all ten fragments with a valid image, so the preamble is not required for a D6 read

defects.item: read-config and backup proved the 144-byte image but recorded nothing about the fragments it was reassembled from
defects.fix: read_config now fills a report dict with the fragment count and per-fragment index, frame size, data size and checksum status; read-config and backup both carry it
defects.regression: three hardware-free tests on the scripted transport plus one CLI payload test

not_done: the live rerun of the research client

next_gate.requirement: a byte-identical no-op D7 round trip, supervised
steps: D6 read back and require an exact byte and SHA match
only then expose a real configuration mutation
